root_cause.text: In `ethosu_gem_cmdstream_copy_and_validate()` in the Ethos-U command stream parser, the loop reuses and increments the `i` buffer index for 64-bit commands without revalidating it against the `bocmds` allocation bounds, allowing a write past the end of the DMA-backed array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (i >= size / 4) return -EINVAL;` immediately after `i++` and before `bocmds[i] = cmds[1];`, and the CVE/commit text explicitly states that when bit 14 is set on the last valid iteration, `i` becomes `size/4` and `bocmds[size/4]` writes four bytes past the `drm_gem_dma_create(ddev, size)` allocation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a post-increment bounds check to reject oversized command streams before writing past the `bocmds` buffer.
intent_record.what: After incrementing the loop/index variable `i`, the code adds a bounds check `if (i >= size / 4) return -EINVAL;` before writing `bocmds[i] = cmds[1];`.
intent_record.how: This prevents the function from writing a second command word into `bocmds` when incrementing `i` would move it past the number of 32-bit entries allowed by `size`, causing the function to fail with `-EINVAL` instead of potentially performing an out-of-bounds write.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is visible in `ethosu_gem_cmdstream_copy_and_validate()`. The loop is bounded only by `for (i = 0; i < size / 4; i++)`, and each iteration writes `bocmds[i] = cmds[0];`. For 64-bit commands, the code checks `if (cmd & 0x4000)`, reads a second word, then does `i++; bocmds[i] = cmds[1]; addr = cmd_to_addr(cmds);`. This reuses and increments the same loop index `i` inside the loop body and performs the second write to `bocmds[i]` without any bounds revalidation after incrementing `i`. If the last iteration enters the `cmd & 0x4000` path when `i` is already at the final valid slot, `i++` advances past the allocated `bocmds` array and `bocmds[i] = cmds[1];` can write out of bounds. No guard such as `if (i + 1 >= size / 4)` is present before the second write, so the vulnerable construct is present. Therefore this code contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.

The vulnerable construct is present in `for (i = 0; i < size / 4; i++) { ... bocmds[i] = cmds[0]; ... if (cmd & 0x4000) { ... i++; bocmds[i] = cmds[1]; ... } }`. The loop condition only validates `i < size / 4` at the top of each iteration. For a 64-bit command near the end of the buffer, the code increments `i` inside the loop (`i++;`) and immediately writes `bocmds[i] = cmds[1];` without any re-check that the new `i` is still within the `bocmds` allocation bounds.
